`verus /work/unionfind_find.rs` now prints `verification results:: 6 verified, 0 errors`. It also prints one warning, which I left alone. The warning says `decreases` checks in exec functions don't guarantee termination of functions with loops or of their callers. It points at `find_rec`, which has no loop.

I only edited the `// <helpers>` and `// <code>` regions. The `// <proofs>` region is unchanged.

- **Body of `find`:** it just calls `self.find_rec(i)`.
- **`find_rec`:** this is the recursive helper, in the helpers region. If the parent of `i` is `i`, it returns `i`. Otherwise it recurses on the parent, then sets `parent[i]` to the root it got back. It has the same `ensures` as `find` and `decreases old(self).measure(i)`.
- **`lemma_root`:** for a valid structure, `spec_find(i)` is in range and is its own root. It is either `i` itself or has strictly higher rank than `i`. This gives the rank invariant after `parent[i]` is changed.
- **`lemma_upd`:** if `parent[i]` is set to `spec_find(i)`, then `spec_find(j)` is unchanged for every `j`. This gives the logical-stability guarantee.

`lemma_upd` is applied to the state after the recursive call, not the original state, because the recursion has already changed some parent pointers.

I used `sed` for the later fixes because Python isn't installed. The first Python patch script I wrote never ran, so I applied that edit by hand.
